title: Deterministic JSON-contract compatibility harness (streaming + constrained decoding)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a reproducible compatibility test harness that validates JSON mode enforcement, constrained-decoding safety, and schema adherence across streaming and function-calling flows. The harness should exercise partial-stream reassembly, deliberate protocol deviations, and backward/forward compatibility against older runtime kernels and client SDKs.
background: We have intermittent customer reports where streaming responses with structured outputs occasionally produce trailing tokens or malformed JSON that pass lightweight validators but fail strict downstream consumers. Existing suites focus on static end-of-response schema checks; we need a deterministic, multi-variant harness that simulates real-world stream fragmentation, interrupted KV-cache warmups, and function/tool calling interleaving to catch regressions before rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run deterministic scenarios that emulate network chunking at configurable byte boundaries
Constrained-decoding layer is exercised with at least 50 fuzzed inputs and must not accept extra-top-level keys when schema forbids them
Streaming reassembly tests cover partial arrays/objects split across 1..8 fragments and ensure the JSON-mode enforcer recovers or fails with clear diagnostics
Compatibility matrix: tests pass (or expected failures documented) across runtime-1.18, runtime-1.20, runtime-1.22 with both new and legacy client SDKs
CI job added to run a representative subset on every PR to the structured-output and streaming-codepaths
Failure output includes a minimal reproducer (seed + chunk boundaries) and a link to a created GH issue template
tasks: Design deterministic chunking API for harness (byte-boundary or token-boundary modes)
Implement streaming reassembly simulator that can inject latency, drop, and reorder fragments
Wire constrained-decoder into harness and add schema fixtures (simple flat objects, nested arrays, union types, function-call payloads)
Create fuzz runner that varies prompt prefix, truncation points, and KV cache warmup behavior
Add test matrix orchestration to run against multiple runtime versions and SDK compatibility shims
Integrate failing-case artifact upload: seed, input prompt, fragment map, runtime logs, and suggested remediation note
Author CI pipeline config and a lightweight README for developers
Run initial sweep and triage top 10 failures into follow-up ENG tickets
test_cases: TC-001: Single-object split into 3 fragments at non-UTF8-safe boundary -> expect error with diagnostic 'incomplete_json_fragment'
TC-002: Array of objects streamed with interleaved function call markers -> decoder must map function-call envelope and produce valid structured output or labeled failure
TC-003: Extra top-level key present when schema.strict=true -> constrained-decoder rejects and returns 'unexpected_field' with field name
TC-004: KV cache cold-start mid-stream where tokenization changes -> streaming runtime must normalize and either continue or abort with graceful fallback
TC-005: Backwards compatibility: runtime-1.18 returns legacy trailing comma tolerance; harness asserts documented deviation and flags as 'compat-allowed' for older runtime
expected_metrics: false_positive_rate < 0.5% for valid payloads when using deterministic chunking
reproducers generated for >= 95% of deterministic failures
CI job time < 15 minutes for smoke subset
fuzz coverage: at least 1e3 unique fragment maps per run
rollout_plan: Merge harness into testing repository behind feature flag. Enable smoke subset on PRs to structured-output and streaming code paths. After two consecutive green runs on runtime-1.22 branch for 48h, enable expanded matrix. Failures auto-file to GH with reproducer and a suggested label. Schedule follow-up bug triage meeting to assign fixes.
rollback_criteria: If >5 production regressions that map to streaming JSON reassembly occur within 7 days of enabling expanded matrix, revert CI gating and create a high-priority incident review.
notes: Prefer seedable pseudo-random generator for fuzzing to ensure reproducibility
Keep harness language-agnostic but provide a thin Python reference runner used by CI
Coordinate with SDK teams for client-side compatibility shims; request two maintainers to validate SDK behavior
We should add schema evolution tests for optional -> required transitions in a follow-up ticket
